1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the Insurance Company challenging by the judgment dated 16.01.2018 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Chickballapur in MVC No.117/2014.
2.

sentences.text: The appellant has challenged the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal on various heads, NC: 2024:KHC:32206 seeking a reduction.
Additionally, they contended that the Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the insured, as the claim petition against the insured was dismissed.
3. None appears for the respondents.
4. The main question raised by the Insurance Company is that the insured was made a party before the Tribunal.
Since the claimant did not take any steps against respondent No.1, i.e., the owner of the offending vehicle, the claim petition against the insured was dismissed.

sentences.text:
5. This Court, in a similar circumstance in MFA No.30255/2011, disposed of on 03.02.2015,
remitted the matter back to the Tribunal to give the claimant an opportunity to take steps against the owner of the offending vehicle.

The relevant paragraphs, Nos. 7 and 8, are hereby extracted for reference:
"7.
A claim petition for compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act has to be filed against the owner of the vehicle and he is a necessary party.

Undisputedly, the claim petition against the owner and the driver came to be NC:
2024:KHC:32206 dismissed as the 1st respondent who was claimant before the tribunal did not take steps to serve the notice to the driver and owner.
Despite the fact that the claim petition was dismissed against the driver and owner, the tribunal has wrongly proceeded against the insurance company.
This approach of the tribunal is improper for the reason that the owner of the vehicle is party to the proceedings.

8. Having had an award in his favour, the 1st respondent herein cannot be non-suited and an opportunity has to be given to him to take appropriate steps to restore the claim petition against the owner/driver.
With this liberty, the impugned judgment and award are set aside.
The matter is remitted back to the tribunal."
6. In view of the above, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the appeal is liable to be allowed and matter is liable to be remitted back to the Tribunal.

Hence, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC:32206 b)
The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is set-aside.
The matter is remanded back to the Tribunal reserving liberty to the claimant to take appropriate steps to restore the claim petition against the insured of the offending vehicle.
c) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal.
d) All the contentions of the parties are kept open.
e) The Tribunal is directed to keep the amount in fixed deposit, in any nationalized bank.

Sd/-
(H.T. NARENDRA PRASAD) JUDGE HA The Manager vs Nirajan on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167777601/
